description: Kernels have no band/bor/bxor/bnot/bsl/bsr (Bitwise module, or the Erlang :erlang.band/2 etc. forms), so hashing and checksum algorithms (CRC32, xxHash, FNV) can't be written; this blocks the checksum example defk-9p6.2. Support them on i64 with Elixir semantics: bsl/bsr are arithmetic with negative shift reversing direction, bsl on i64 must raise or match Elixir for results outside i64 (Elixir has bignums; decide: raise ArithmeticError on overflow like + - *), bnot is two's complement. Accept both `import Bitwise` operator forms (&&&, |||, ^^^, <<<, >>>, ~~~) and band/2-style calls. Tests compare with Elixir, including negative values and shift edge cases (shift >= 64, negative shift).

comments.text: Per 'Should kernels offer opt-in wrapping integer arithmetic for hashes?' (defk-dtw.10): scope now also covers masked arithmetic (band(expr, 2^k-1) with + - * bsl band bor bxor bnot inside, computed wrapping; bsr/div/rem only on in-range values; syntactic recognition), the u64 scalar and [u64] element type with its mixing rules, and Defk.Bits (clz, ctz, popcount, rotl, rotr). See the resolution comment on defk-dtw.10.

title: Support bitwise operators in kernels
